understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call searching for what it's all for, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: The quiet house is not a void but a doorway. Over seven days you will find the Gita not as a set of forwarded verses, but as a conversation that begins with your own life.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Near the end, Krishna tells Arjuna that a busy, working life is no barrier.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
verse.line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
verse.translation: Even while always doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal, imperishable home by my grace.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.meaning: Near the end of the teaching, Krishna speaks to Arjuna. They are standing at the edge of a great battle, and Arjuna is asking what a person should do when the ground beneath them shifts. Krishna says that it does not matter how many tasks fill your days. Even while doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal home by my grace. The verse says that your actions do not block the way. What you do, you do while holding onto the one who holds everything.
verse.for_you: You have spent a lifetime doing work. Now the house is quiet, and you have the time to sit with the Gita. Let this be your work today. Read a verse, and let it be your leaning. The quiet is not an empty space.

verse.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verse.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verse.sanskrit: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verse.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
verse.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.meaning: A teacher once asked a student to look at the self that lives inside the heart and visits them every night in deep sleep, though they never recognize it. The student kept looking, and the teacher said that people are like those who walk every day over a buried treasure of gold and never find it. They pass their own treasure every day and never find it, carried away by untruth.
verse.for_you: The quiet house and the verses you read are the ground beneath your feet. You have been walking past your own meaning every day. The Gita is not a treasure to find elsewhere, but the ground you have always stood on.

verse.speaker: Sumantra
verse.setting: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.
verse.sanskrit: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
verse.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.
verse.translation: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
verse.meaning: After a long night, the charioteer Sumantra returned alone to the grieving king Dasharath and held him. He said that birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad. The steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
verse.for_you: The quiet of the house is not a void but a doorway. The stillness is not an absence but a presence you have always walked past.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Senajit (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: Vyasa quotes the grieving King Senajit to Yudhishthira, who is broken by the war's losses.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च / लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च / पर्यायतः सर्वमवाप्तुवन्ति / तस्मान्न मुह्येन्न च संप्रहृष्येत्
verse.line: Gain and loss, joy and sorrow come to everyone in turn. Don't be crushed, and don't get carried away.
verse.translation: Happiness and sorrow, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: everyone receives all of these in turn. So do not be thrown off by them, and do not get carried away either.
verse.why: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.

prasang.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
prasang.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
prasang.story_hook: He had won the war, and all Yudhishthira wanted was to walk into the forest and never come back.
prasang.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.

verse.meaning: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira about King Senajit, who has lost everything. Senajit sits in his quiet palace and says that gain and loss, joy and sorrow, come to everyone like day and night. He asks his family to hold both alike, without being crushed by grief or carried away by joy. The verse tells us that the good we do next counts, even when we feel broken.
verse.for_you: The quiet house holds both the loss and the time you have now. Hold them both. The grief is real, and your next step still counts. The stillness is not an end. It is the ground you stand on to do what comes next.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna opens the teaching on knowing him fully.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
verse.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
verse.translation: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.

verse.meaning: Krishna is opening up the teaching on how to know him completely. He tells Arjuna that if they keep their mind attached to him, practice the discipline of yoga, and take refuge in him, they will come to know him fully and without any doubt. It is a promise that steady attention and trust will lead to understanding, not a sudden flash but a deepening.
verse.for_you: You have time now to sit with a verse and let it settle. When the house is quiet, try resting your attention on one line and see what it says to you before you move to the next. Let the words stay with you for a while.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna begins his ladder of practices with the simplest instruction.
verse.sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
verse.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
verse.translation: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna as they stand on the field of war. He offers a ladder of practices, starting with the simplest step. Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me. This means to make your focus a single place. Let your understanding rest there. Then you will truly dwell in that place, and nothing will shake you. It is not about forcing your thoughts, but about choosing where they settle.
verse.for_you: The house is quiet now. Let your mind rest in that quiet for a few minutes this evening. Do not try to fill it. Let your thinking settle there, and see what comes next.

story.title: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything
story.story_hook: The prince who had everything came back from his travels and stopped laughing.
story.summary: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
story.lesson: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.

story.for_you: Rama had everything and came back empty. You are not ill. You are asking the first real questions. Let someone help you through it.

script: The house is very quiet now. You have spent a lifetime filling the hours with work. Now the hours are yours, and the quiet is heavy. You are not looking for a problem to fix. You are looking for what comes next.

Krishna and Arjuna stand near the edge of a vast plain. Arjuna has laid down his bow. He is asking what a person should do when everything they knew changes. Krishna looks at the armies and speaks to him about work and grace, about doing what must be done while holding on. Krishna said:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः, मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्.
In plain words: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.

The verse says that your actions do not block the way. You can be busy, and still you can reach the lasting home. It is not about stopping your work. It is about leaning on the one who holds everything while you do it. This is easier said than done, because after a lifetime of doing, to do nothing feels like falling. But Krishna says the work itself is not the barrier. The leaning is. It is not a feeling. It is a direction.
You have time now after retiring. Let the Gita be your work today. Read a verse, and let it be your leaning. The quiet is not an empty space. It is the place where you can hear the words clearly.
What if your work was simply to read and rest?

depth.life: The house is quiet after your wife passed away. You have time now after retiring, but the silence does not feel like peace. You are looking for what this time is for, and you want to read the Gita on your own terms, not as a forwarded message.
depth.points: Work is not the only path. Even in action, one can lean on the lasting home. The search for meaning is not a problem to fix. It is the quiet ground where a different kind of work begins.
depth.practice: Choose one small task today, like making tea, and do it while holding the thought that this is your work. Let your mind rest there.
depth.question: What feels like work to you in this quiet house?
